title: RSF-SPLM-N Dawn Assault on Kurmuk's Al-Baraka Repelled as Joint Force Reinforces Ed Damazin
detail: Sudanese army and allied forces repelled a dawn assault by the RSF-SPLM-N alliance — led by Joseph Touka — on the Al-Baraka area of Al-Kurmuk locality, Blue Nile state, on Friday, September 4, 2026, inflicting what Al-Kurmuk town authorities described as heavy losses in personnel and equipment, destroying several combat vehicles and forcing the remaining fighters to withdraw toward the Ethiopian border; the claims could not be independently verified and the RSF made no immediate comment. The clash came as the rebel coalition threatened a renewed advance on Blue Nile's state capital, Ed Damazin, prompting the army to rush reinforcements — including elements of the Darfur Joint Force — into the city from Khartoum, Gezira, and Sennar states, days after the RSF-SPLM-N alliance claimed capture of the army's Bakori and Sirkam bases on August 28 and two days after Sovereignty Council chief Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan inspected the 4th Infantry Division in Damazin.

sources.name: Sudan Tribune — Clashes erupt in Sudan's Blue Nile as rebel alliance advances toward Ed Damazin
Anadolu Agency — Sudanese army says it repelled RSF attack in Blue Nile state

media.caption: The Sudanese army said it repelled an RSF-SPLM-N dawn assault on the Al-Baraka area of Kurmuk locality on September 4, 2026, as reinforcements poured into Ed Damazin.

confidenceReason: Battlefield claim by Sudanese army/Al-Kurmuk town authorities, reported independently by two Tier-2 wire/outlet sources, but not independently verified and the RSF did not respond.

title: SPLM-N Forces Kill 21+ Otoro Villagers in Debi and Luwairi Near Kauda, Violating August Ceasefire
detail: SPLM-N (al-Hilu faction) fighters attacked the villages of Debi and Luweri, south and west of Kauda in South Kordofan's Nuba Mountains, on Thursday, September 4, 2026, killing more than 21 people — including women and children — from the Otoro ethnic minority and wounding at least 11 others, according to the Sudan Doctors Network. The group said the attack 'constitute[d] a clear violation of the [late-August ceasefire] agreement, a resumption of hostilities, and the targeting of civilians on an ethnic basis,' and that at least 158 people have been killed in SPLM-N operations against Otoro communities since violence there erupted in March 2026. Al-Hilu's SPLM-N never committed to an RSF-backed ceasefire initiative launched in August and had already struck at least 10 Otoro villages between August 20-26, displacing thousands of civilians.
